svg.text: Beginner • Exam-style revision • Three lecture parts
TAKEAWAY: compare sample evidence with a pre-set rule, then weigh the cost of both error types.
→ = leads to / next step [S1] errors & power [S2] statistic & business tests [S3] α, p-values & coin test
[S1] What would count as an effect?
[S2] Ask how unusual the evidence is under H₀.
Compare p with α → decide → weigh error costs
[S3] Decision informs action; it does not prove H₀.
Arrow = logical flow, not proof of cause.
Risk: act on a false link.
WHAT: chance of rejecting H₀ when it is false.
FORMULA: power = 1 − β; β = Type II error.
WHY / EXAMPLE: detect a real coin bias more often.
More power = better chance to detect a real effect
Trade-off: easier rejection can raise Type I risk.
Statistic = summary number from the sample.
Null distribution = expected statistics if H₀ is true.
Compare the observed value with that distribution.
Choose BEFORE seeing results: the threshold for rejecting H₀.
Smaller α lowers Type I risk, but may lower power.
Choose based on error costs (e.g., medication vs ad font size).
Never change α just to get a preferred result → P-hacking.
Probability of the observed result OR something more extreme,
assuming H₀ is true. Tail(s) depend on the alternative H₁.
p > α → FAIL TO REJECT H₀
Not the probability that H₀ is true.
QUESTION: Is the coin biased toward producing fewer heads? [S3]
Coin has fewer heads than fair expectation
Not extreme enough to reject H₀ at this cutoff.
This does NOT prove the coin is fair.
I: reject true H₀; II: miss a real effect.
Churn: false link = I; missed link = II. [S1]
α set first; p calculated from sample.
Never tune α after seeing p. [S3]
Not enough evidence to reject H₀.
Transcript says coin p is above “0.5”; context suggests α = 0.05, but the typo is unconfirmed.
Worked example uses α = 0.05. “α = 0.00” is mentioned but is not a useful conventional cutoff.
The confidence-interval “acceptance region” description is an oversimplification.
Type II: fail to reject false H₀.
p > α: fail to reject H₀.
ACTIVE RECALL • COVER THE ANSWERS FIRST
3. What is power, and how does β relate to it?
4. If α = 0.05 and p = 0.03, what is the decision?
5. If p = 0.12 and α = 0.05, what is the decision?
6. Why calculate P(X ≤ 3), not only P(X = 3), for H₁: p < 0.5?
7. Why choose α before inspecting results?
8. Give one Type I and one Type II churn mistake.
Type II: fail to reject false H₀.
H₁ points to 3 or fewer heads.
Churn: false link = I; missed true link = II.
